title: Holly leaf motif
subtitle: A spiky flat holly leaf in dark green with optional red berry French knots, 8 cm
excerpt: The holly leaf is worked around a centre spine with sharp alternating points along each side — three deep indentations with spike-tip trebles between them. At 8 cm in DK cotton the spiky profile is unmistakable. Add three red French-knot berries at the base for the classic Christmas motif, or leave it plain for a year-round botanical applique.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (1889), Christmas botanical motif chapter (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet holiday motif section.
heroPrompt: A crochet holly leaf applique in dark green DK cotton with three red berry French knots at the base, 8 cm long with six visible spiky points, photographed flat on white cotton in soft daylight.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished holly leaf measures 8 cm long and 4 cm wide in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.

chartDefinition.title: Holly leaf motif
chartDefinition.caption: Centre spine chain. Three spike points per side: treble at the spike tip, sl-st at the indentation between spikes. Pointed tip at leaf end.

glossaryTerms.definition: A slip stitch worked between spike points on a holly leaf, pulling the outline inward at each notch to create the characteristic deeply lobed holly shape.

content.text: The holly leaf alternates treble spike tips with
slip stitch indentations

along both sides of a centre spine chain, giving the deeply cut three-spike-per-side profile. The tip is a 3dc rounded turn. The base returns to the stem with a slip stitch close. Red berry French knots are optional — three clustered at the stem end in red embroidery thread.

attrs.title: Materials for one leaf
attrs.body: About 6 g of dark green DK cotton. A 4 mm hook. Tapestry needle. Red embroidery thread for berries (optional). Scissors.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished holly leaf measures 8 cm long and 4 cm wide in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook.
Stitches used
chain (ch), slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc) — UK; US "single crochet".
treble (tr) — UK; US "double crochet." Used at each spike tip.
Pattern
Foundation
Ch 14. Sl st into the 2nd ch from hook (stem base).
First side — 3 spikes

Dc in next ch. Tr in next ch (spike 1). Dc in next ch. Sl st in next ch (indentation). Dc in next ch. Tr in next ch (spike 2). Dc in next ch. Sl st in next ch (indentation). Dc in next ch. Tr in next ch (spike 3). Dc in next ch.
Leaf tip
3dc in the final chain to turn the leaf tip.
Return side — 3 spikes
Working back along the underside of the spine: Dc. Tr (spike). Dc. Sl st (indentation). Dc. Tr (spike). Dc. Sl st (indentation). Dc. Tr (spike). Dc. Sl st to close at the stem base. Fasten off.

definition.title: Holly leaf motif
definition.caption: 14ch spine. 3 spike points (tr) per side with sl-st indentations between. 3dc at tip. Stem sl-st.

content.text: Finishing
Weave in ends. Add three red French knot berries at the stem base using red embroidery thread if desired. Sew the holly leaf onto the base fabric.
Care
Handwash in cool water. Lay flat to dry. The spike points may need a light press with a damp cloth to restore sharpness.
What to try next

The snowflake motifs (crochet-snowflake-basic, crochet-snowflake-intricate) pair with holly for a full Christmas applique set. The basic snowflake (crochet-snowflake-basic) is the natural companion for a festive garland.
